newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices flat, tone firmer.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices flat, tone firmer.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds opened flat but with a firmer bias as light supply painted a promising technical picture.

"I'd say we are pretty flat on the day so far," a trader said, adding that the market had a good tone. Deals so far this week -- including a $514 million Anaheim, Calif., offering -- were well received, and the secondary market has traded "pretty well," he said.

"I think that the market had gotten kind of oversold, and I don't think there was a lot of paper around," the trader said. "Remember we had those weeks of lots of heavy selling. I don't think they were ever able to buy anything back, and I think they are starting to buy it back at maybe higher prices."
A second trader said the market opened firmer, though action was light. He also cited light supply.
"There's nothing around and the market will be driven because of that," he said. "There's no supply in the primary market (and) very few bonds in the secondary."
Though they have "plenty of cash," buyers have seen the U.S. Treasury market run "so much, so fast" that they believe a correction could occur.
"So they are wishing the market down," the trader said. "That might not happen."
Given munis lack of supply, if the government market improves again, "most of that money will go to work," the trader said.
In debt futures, the March municipal contract was up 8/32 at 116-6/32. The March T-bond contract was up 7/32 at 112-14/32. The MOB spread was 120 ticks.
In the government cash market, the benchmark 30-year bond was up 6/32 at 97-17/32 To yield 6.69 percent.

On the economic front, the Commerce Department issues December factory orders at 1000 EST. The Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee is set to disclose policy following a two-day meeting at approximately 1415 EST.
